messages:
incident-bot: Paging: KV cache pressure + continuous-batching regression detected. Spikes in p95 token latency and autoscale oscillation in eu-west-1. Severity: P2. Incident channel created.

Jordan: saw the alert. p95s jumped from ~120ms to 900ms, error rate on streaming replies up ~3%. autoscaler HPA churn visible.

Mina: on it. I'm rolling back the recent batching tweak for the model pool 'redwood-medium-v2' to previous config. Will update when done.

Samir: what config specifically? the changes to continuous_batch.size?

Mina: yes. Reverted continuous_batch.max_size from 64 -> 16 and disabled aggressive warmup. applying now.

Mina: applying rollback:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://control-plane.local/api/pools/redwood-medium-v2/config -d '{"continuous_batch": {"max_size": 16, "warmup_enabled": false}}'
```

Jordan: seeing partial drop in p95 already on one host. KV cache entries also down from 1.8M -> 400k on node-23.

Zara: customer-facing: some requests are timing out in EU, small percent of requests get 504s. Logged in support queue. Tagging accounts with heavy streaming usage.

Hana: FYI HPA started launching new pods every ~45s because CPU probe jumped as KV cache warmed — leads to thrash. We should bump stabilization window.

Samir: agree. temp fix: increase hpa.spec.behavior.stabilizationWindowSeconds to 300 for affected deployment and set maxScaleDown to 1 to avoid simultaneous flapping.

Mina: doing HPA change now.
```yaml
# patch
- op: replace
  path: /spec/behavior/scaleDown/stabilizationWindowSeconds
  value: 300
```

Mina: patched. pods are not terminating as fast, scaling looks calmer.

Jordan: metrics: p95 now ~220ms, error rate down to 0.6%. Still above baseline but trending good.

ops-bot: Deploybot: config rollback succeeded for pool redwood-medium-v2 at 1719903608.

Zara: prepping short customer note: "We observed transient latency and timeouts in EU for streaming responses due to an internal batching change. We have rolled back the change and scaled stabilizers; services are recovering." Sending to SCS in 10m unless more impact.

Ryan_P: thanks — notify any customers on dedicated/Dedicated+ who had reserved throughput; they may see degraded SLA. I'll coordinate with Sales.

Samir: root cause hypothesis: the aggressive continuous batching increased KV cache working set; warmup created hot prefixes -> nodes spike CPU and OOM-ish behaviour causing HPA wrong signals. cumulative effect -> autoscale thrash.

Mina: adding a safety: limit per-worker KV cache memory to 8GB and enable prefix-dedupe for warmup. Applying policy.

Jordan: logs excerpt from node-23: 
```
[2024-07-02T14:33:12Z] warn: kv_cache_eviction: entries=1_809_012 memory=14.2GB
[2024-07-02T14:33:15Z] error: rpc_stream_timings p95=912ms error_rate=3.2%
[2024-07-02T14:33:17Z] info: hpa_scale_event: old_replicas=3 new_replicas=6 reason=cpu
```

Hana: good logs. I'll create a follow-up runbook item: ensure warmup ramp is tied to observed KV memory and not time-based.

Zara: SCS note queued. I'll CC customers with >1M requests/day.

ops-bot: Incident timeline updated. Incident severity remains P2.

Samir: recommend retro actions: add canary flag for batching experiments, add KV working-set alarm, and change HPA to use custom metric 'inference_cpu_stable' that smooths short spikes.

Jordan: ok I'll draft the incident write-up. Mina, please hand off remaining watch to Hana in 20m.

Mina: handing off to Hana now. I've attached my checklist in case: rollback applied, HPA patched, per-worker KV cap set, prefix-dedupe enabled, monitoring dashboards pinned.

Hana: acknowledged. I'll monitor for 2 hours and then escalate back if p95 > 400ms for >5m or error_rate >1%.

Zara: customer note sent at 1719903710.

Jordan: good job team. Adding this to postmortem queue and scheduling a follow-up demo of batching config safety knobs. :thumbsup:

Hana: oncall takeover confirmed. Closing active paging loop.
